per_task.rationale: The DB went from dirty (md5 3a66…) before the run to seed (md5 a592…) after, matching instance_seed. The authenticated POST /reset/amazon returned 200, and the reset events show 'called' then 'database_restored'. Both homepage GETs had authorization=null. Exit code was 0, and the token does not appear in stdout or stderr.

The only reset request was POST /reset-all (200, partial=false). No /reset/<site> request was made. The DB went from dirty to seed, the reset events show 'database_restored', exit code was 0, and the token was not printed.

No --db-root or --docker-container flag was passed (options no_source=true). A checkout DB existed and was dirty (checkout-before/state.json). The reset returned 200 and the deploy DB was restored. The CLI reported md5_status=SKIP with md5_source='none' and did not use the checkout DBs. Exit code was 0 and the token was not printed.

No client token was set. The control requests went out without authorization and got 401. There were no reset events, and the DB stayed dirty with the same hash before and after. The CLI reported health and reset as FAIL, parity as SKIP, and exited 1.

With the wrong token, both /health and /reset/amazon returned 401. There were no reset events and the DB stayed dirty. The CLI reported reset FAIL and parity SKIP, and exited 1. Neither the wrong token nor the server token appears in stdout or stderr.

With the wrong token, POST /reset-all returned 401 and no per-site reset was attempted. There were no reset events and the DB stayed dirty. The CLI reported reset FAIL and parity SKIP, exited 1, and did not print the token.

The token 'short' was rejected with a structured JSON error ('at least 32 printable ASCII characters'). The HTTP log is empty, the redirect listener log is empty, there were no reset events, and the DB was unchanged. Exit code was 1 and the token was not printed.

A token containing a newline and an injected header was rejected with a structured JSON error. No HTTP requests were made, there were no reset events, and the DB was unchanged. Exit code was 1 and neither the token nor the injected text appears in stdout.

A 32-character non-ASCII token was rejected with a structured JSON error. No HTTP requests were made, there were no reset events, and the DB was unchanged. Exit code was 1 and the token was not printed.

Authenticated /health and /reset/amazon got 302 responses pointing to the listener at 127.0.0.1:56509. The CLI treated both as FAIL and did not follow them: the listener recorded no requests. There were no reset events, the DB stayed dirty, and exit code was 1.

The homepage request to / got a 302 to /landing, which returned 200. Both times, both hops had authorization=null. The home check is PASS, the authenticated reset returned 200, and the DB was restored to seed. The redirect listener received nothing and exit code was 0.

A token of exactly 32 printable ASCII characters was sent as a Bearer header and accepted with 200 on /health and /reset/amazon. The DB was restored to seed, exit code was 0, and the token does not appear in stdout.

The authenticated reset got a 503 from the backend. The reset events show only 'called', with no restore. The DB stayed dirty with the same hash before and after. The CLI reported reset FAIL and parity SKIP, exited 1, and did not print the token.

limitations: The results cover guided loopback fixture runs with a single site. The process lifecycle was stubbed and the control redirect was a wrapper fixture (per environment.json).
I did not open manifest.json or verify_packet.py directly. The hash and SQLite checks are trusted from the script's exit-0 'VERIFIED' output.
The token-leak check covers only stdout.json and stderr.txt as captured. Logs and other outputs outside the packet were not examined.

In A04, with no token set, the CLI still sent unauthenticated control requests instead of stopping before sending anything. The contract only requires failure with the DB unchanged, so this is noted but does not fail the task.
This verdict does not certify source correctness, Docker or full-site deployment, browser behavior, or any scenario outside this packet.
